observations.explanation: The paper says tasks have natural-language instructions, initial-state setup configurations, and manually crafted execution scripts (PDF pp. 7–8); it also describes intermediate states and execution-based checks (pp. 4–5).
Human performance is reported as approximately 72.36%, alongside model results, and the paper explicitly contrasts this with much lower baseline performance (PDF pp. 9–11).

The authors report further red-teaming could reduce false positives and negatives and defer that work, while describing multiple rounds of quality checks (PDF pp. 7–8). The claim appropriately presents this as a caveat rather than invalidating all scores.

The 369-task public benchmark is Ubuntu-based; the paper provides a smaller 43-task Windows set, and says macOS was not used for benchmark development due to copyright concerns (PDF pp. 6, 26–27). The stated generalization question is appropriately unresolved.
